### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6fd87b7e82f7e60f3417649f4831984eeaa38148` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `453285369442d32cc1354b8d67cb0174c7836dee` — the merge of head `538fc2a257d0380e03dab14e94e4c64bcd3d3e45` into base `6fd87b7e82f7e60f3417649f4831984eeaa38148`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 453285369442d32cc1354b8d67cb0174c7836dee && git checkout 453285369442d32cc1354b8d67cb0174c7836dee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6fd87b7e82f7e60f3417649f4831984eeaa38148 538fc2a257d0380e03dab14e94e4c64bcd3d3e45 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6fd87b7e82f7e60f3417649f4831984eeaa38148 && git merge --no-ff 538fc2a257d0380e03dab14e94e4c64bcd3d3e45

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6fd87b7e82f7e60f3417649f4831984eeaa38148
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6fd87b7e82f7e60f3417649f4831984eeaa38148` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `538fc2a257d0380e03dab14e94e4c64bcd3d3e45`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/preview-evaluator.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/preview-undeclared-measure-parity.test.ts, .changeset/28172-preview-undeclared-measure.md + packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-refusal.ts (`invalidMemberError`), packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-executor.ts (`runMeasurePass`, bare measure names), packages/services/service-analytics/src/index.ts (barrel), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/DatasetPreview.tsx, packages/client/src/index.ts (`queryDataset` options)

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset, both line-initial, both arms match). No governed path in the 4-file list; no published schema touched.
- (1) Parity, read off the diff: the preview query proxy now runs `mintCallerMeasures` → `assertMeasureFields` → `assertCallerMeasuresResolvable` → `assertMeasureFieldTypes` → body/internal/field-read/currency gates → evaluator, all over the cube WITH the minted measures, as `ensureCube` does on the live path (augmented branch). `nope`/`ghost_avg` are refused by the same `assertMeasureFields` method with the same message text (INVALID_FIELD/400, `param`/`field`/`measure` set), and the test pins the preview message byte-equal to native and ObjectQL. `region_sum` → same `assertCubeMeasureFieldTypesAccepted` door (400); `amount + 1` → same `fieldReadUnjudgeableError` (403); `secret_sum` → the existing `assertFieldsReadable` now sees the minted measure's field (403, `fields: ['secret']`), pinned on preview and native. Declared `total` and undeclared `count` serve the same values on all three faces (CONTROL cells); a legitimately minted `amount_sum` / bare `amount` now serves `SUM(amount)` on the preview as live does (a value change from the old row count, stated in the changeset).
- (2) Live faces: `mintCallerMeasures` is the `ensureCube` loop moved verbatim (same skip order: declared key, duration measure, `mintableMeasureKey`, `inferMeasure` with the `#21437` refusal); `assertCallerMeasuresResolvable` is the measure half of `assertCallerMembersResolvable` with `durations` passed in instead of read from `scope`, called from the same spot with the same probe/author cube. Behaviour-neutral on native/ObjectQL/`generateSql`; the dev's full-package run (198 files, 0 failed) and the pinned live columns agree.
- (3) The three extra gates are the live path's own refusals (`#21156`, `#21044`, field-level read), not new rules: each refusal the preview now gives is one native/ObjectQL already give for the same spelling, and each is pinned across the three faces with an ablation. They are within the triage rule ("refuses ... with the live faces' envelope"), read as parity; the PR body says the seat confirmed that reading. Declared in the changeset as part of the one narrowing.
- (4) Clause-② re-derived: no new export (`mintCallerMeasures`, `undeclaredPreviewMeasureError` module-private; `assertCallerMeasuresResolvable` a private method; barrel unchanged), no new answer member, no new status or code (`INVALID_FIELD`/400 via the existing `invalidMemberError`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`/403 existing). `no (narrowing)` holds; nothing makes it `yes`.
- (6) Clients: `ui` `DatasetPreview.tsx` sends only the draft dataset's own declared `measures[].name`; `DatasetWidget`/`ObjectChart`/report renderer name declared dataset measures; `packages/client` `queryDataset` passes `previewDrafts` through with no measure shaping. No client, doc or skill relies on the preview counting an undeclared measure (`git grep previewDrafts` over ui/, packages/client, content/docs, skills).
- (7) Undeclared DIMENSION: not covered here (`assertDimensionFields` is not asked on the preview); the PR says so and it is filed as #28201. Correct to leave it.
- Evaluator: the `count(*)` fallback is gone (`if (!metric) throw`), with duration measures still handled first; the only production caller hands over the minted cube. Existing direct-evaluator tests declare `count` on their cube, so they keep passing.
- Check-runs at head: 12 success, 13 skipped, 20 in progress at review time (Test Core 1-8, Build Core, Lint, Type Check). Dev reports the package suite, typecheck, lint and all 62 dispatch-gate families green at head.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/service-analytics`: `patch` with BREAKING banner, `!` title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — matches AGENTS.md (a non-protocol narrowing ships patch and keeps its banner and disposition). The changeset body carries Before/Now/remedy, no FROM → TO code rewrite, so the `no-migration-prescription` arm is consistent; the gate's own run is in the pending CI.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Accept-set narrowing on one face only: `queryDataset` with `previewDrafts: true` over a pending seed draft. Refusals are the live faces' existing envelopes; no new boundary, code, status or export.
- Value change on the same face for an inferred measure over a real field (row count → live aggregate), declared in the changeset.
- Live native/ObjectQL/`generateSql` paths: unchanged.
- Out of scope, filed: undeclared dimension on the preview (#28201).

### ④ Design judgment

- The narrowing makes the published contract's own refusal real on the preview rather than taking a capability away: a Studio author sees the same refusal (same text) before publishing that the published dataset answers after. One mint loop and one caller-measure gate shared by both faces means the two cannot drift again on these spellings.
- Non-blocking note: gate order on the preview (`#21156` 403 before the field-type 400 and the currency door) differs from `ensureCube` (field-type and currency before the 403). Both faces refuse a query that trips two of them, but may name a different mistake first. No pinned single-mistake case is affected; reordering to `ensureCube`'s order is a small follow-up, not a must-fix.
- Dimension half deliberately left to #28201; the preview still serves an undeclared dimension as one `null` group until then.

> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；

> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；

> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
